summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's intrinsic behavior, output format, tone, or domain-specific reasoning in ways that prompting and RAG cannot achieve, or when you want to reduce latency and cost by baking knowledge into the weights. RAG is better when you need up-to-date or frequently changing factual knowledge, while prompt engineering is the cheapest first step for most tasks. Reach for fine-tuning only after prompting and RAG plateau on a well-defined, high-volume task with stable requirements.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, style, or tone that few-shot prompting cannot reliably enforce across thousands of calls.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the required knowledge changes often or must be auditable/citable, since RAG keeps facts external and updatable.
Fine-tune for domain adaptation or specialized reasoning (legal, medical, code) where the base model lacks the necessary behavior even with rich context.
Use fine-tuning to cut inference cost and latency by shrinking long system prompts into learned weights for a stable, high-throughput task.
